scope: CR02 3.1.0 candidate recheck of the UniApp lock and DCloud/Vite support matrix; no arbitrary dependency migration, runtime service, public development server or production claim.

local_facts.direct_high: vite@5.2.8 aggregates current development-server and launch-editor advisories; npm proposes vite@5.4.21 outside the installed plugin's exact peer

official_sources.fact: The installed plugin metadata still declares peerDependencies.vite exactly 5.2.8.
The current npm vue3 dist-tag resolves to 3.0.0-alpha-1000920260909822 and declares Vite exactly 8.2.2.
DCloud documents separate stable and alpha Vue3/Vite CLI tracks; changing tracks requires coordinated DCloud-family compatibility validation rather than a Vite-only override.

known_supported: The installed DCloud family supports only Vite 5.2.8. A newer official vue3 pre-release track supports Vite 8.2.2, but it changes the coordinated DCloud toolchain family and is not a drop-in lock repair for this candidate.
inference: Forcing Vite 5.4.21 or 8.2.2 under the installed plugin would violate its exact peer. Moving the complete application to the newer pre-release DCloud family is a separate compatibility change that needs focused H5 and mini-program build/runtime qualification; CR02 does not silently broaden into that migration.
decision: The next-candidate trigger has been satisfied with a fresh lock audit and current registry metadata. Preserve the installed vendor-supported family and the existing bounded controls: build-only use, no public development server, no vulnerability-free claim. The high finding remains an explicitly accepted, time-bounded build/development risk through 2026-10-09; a DCloud-family migration must be separately qualified before that date or the next candidate, whichever comes first.
uncertainties: The vue3 dist-tag is a pre-release track and is not evidence that this application's H5 and mini-program targets are compatible without migration testing.
The audit severity aggregates transitive findings; this review does not claim production Runtime exposure or zero exploitability.
Real Provider and customer deployment qualification remain outside CR02.
